correctness.rationale: The party-list TU worth is derived exactly from proportional seat caps and three possible two-seat allocations; Shapley predecessor sums reduce to rational binomial sums and yield efficient payoffs. A complete finite certificate checks all 49 party-size splits through 14 voters, all 1512 coalition-composition inequalities, and reproduces the value independently from labelled predecessor subsets. At (6,8), the unique failing type is (6,1), with exact Shapley payoff 5065/858 against worth 6, gap 83/858. No statement is made for n>14.

originality.rationale: Originality concerns only the minimal two-disjoint-homogeneous-party, two-seat TU-PAV Shapley-core failure at 14 voters, not the general phenomenon. Chen–Hatschka (arXiv:2605.22528) show a 4-voter overlapping-profile non-core Shapley allocation; Brill–Laslier–Skowron (arXiv:1611.08691) show party-list PAV/D'Hondt winner correspondence. Full primary texts of both were inspected and neither implies the sharp restricted threshold. Targeted research-record and public-literature searches found no directly covering statement; risk from unindexed/indirect equivalent work remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent enumeration or an implication from less easily found TU cooperative-game literature could have established the same exact finite cutoff

value.rationale: A sharply delimited and natural restricted approval domain tests whether a TU-Shapley coalition-stability defect survives after all cross-party approval overlap is removed. Its first possible failure shifts from a known 4-voter overlapping example to 14 voters, with a unique six-plus-one blocking composition. This provides a nontrivial complete finite structural boundary, not a restatement of winner apportionment or an arbitrary table entry.
